objective: Create tests/test_wire_contract.py (new) with 5 stdlib-unittest tests pinning frozen C1 and C2 at unit level — producer emits 'timeout_ms' and never 'timeout'; engine.run_job decides 'done'/'timeout' from 'timeout_ms' per C2; consumer.job_timeout resolves 'timeout_ms' first, then the 'timeout' fallback, then the 30000 default — so any future drift on seams S1/S2 fails the suite.

concepts: job wire format and C1 key precedence (DA-1)
C2 engine comparison semantics (work_ms > timeout_ms; boundary work_ms == timeout_ms → 'done')
existing unittest module style (TestX(unittest.TestCase) + module-level main guard)

inputs: DA-1 decision (defines the fallback behavior the tests pin)
tests/test_producer.py and tests/test_consumer.py as style references (read-only)
non_goals: Do not modify any pipeline/ file — production code is read-only for this task
Do not edit tests/test_producer.py, tests/test_consumer.py, or tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py
Do not create files outside owned_paths (no tests/integration/ — that is T03)
implementation_constraints: Stdlib unittest only; the module must run via python -m unittest tests.test_wire_contract from the repo root

Exactly 5 test methods: (1) producer emits 'timeout_ms' with the passed value and no 'timeout' key; (2) engine.run_job returns 'done' at work 50 and 'timeout' at work 150 for timeout_ms=100; (3) consumer.job_timeout(make_job(..., timeout_ms=500)) returns 500; (4) consumer.job_timeout({'timeout': 123}) returns 123 (draft-key fallback per DA-1); (5) consumer.job_timeout({}) returns 30000 (default)
Write the consumer-resolution assertions against the frozen C1 spec, not against T01's in-progress code
No new dependencies; follow the existing test-module docstring and naming style

deliverables.what: wire-contract regression suite, 5 tests pinning C1/C2

acceptance_tests.description: The module collects and runs exactly 5 tests; the required green set (producer-key, engine, fallback, default tests) reports OK in every state. State-conditional on T01: if T01 has not yet landed, the consumer-resolution test may be red (exactly 1 failure expected per T02-AT4); 'Ran 5 tests ... OK' with exit code 0 is required only when T01 is present; red/green state recorded in checkpoints/T02.json
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_wire_contract -v → 5 tests collected; producer-key, engine, fallback, default tests OK; if T01 not yet landed: exactly 1 failure on the consumer-resolution test (per T02-AT4), otherwise 'Ran 5 tests ... OK', exit code 0; state recorded in checkpoints/T02.json

acceptance_tests.description: The producer-key test pins make_job output: assertEqual(job['timeout_ms'], 500) and assertNotIn('timeout', job) both pass
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_wire_contract -v → the producer-key test reports OK

acceptance_tests.description: If the consumer-resolution test were written against the draft key only (e.g. asserting job_timeout({'timeout_ms': 500}) returns 30000), the suite fails — the test must encode the C1 chain, not the old draft behavior
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_wire_contract -v → FAIL on the consumer-resolution test when the C1 chain is not encoded

acceptance_tests.description: While T01 has not yet landed in the working tree, the consumer-resolution test (job_timeout(make_job(..., timeout_ms=500)) returns 500) is red — the expected TDD state for a test written in parallel against a frozen spec; it must be green once T01 is complete (asserted by T04 in A4)
acceptance_tests.evidence: Run before T01 lands: exactly 1 failure, on the consumer-resolution test. Run after T01 lands: 'Ran 5 tests ... OK'. Both states are recorded in the T02 checkpoint.

failure_cases.scenario: T01 lands after T02 in the same working tree (parallel group, order not guaranteed)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: T02's consumer-resolution test turns green without any test edit; T02 records the red→green state change in its checkpoint

failure_cases.scenario: A future change makes the producer emit 'timeout' alongside or instead of 'timeout_ms'
failure_cases.expected_behavior: The producer-key test fails (assertNotIn / assertEqual), flagging the C1 drift immediately

handoff.notes: Checkpoint must record: the module's red/green state at completion (which of the 5 tests were red and why — expected: only the consumer-resolution test, red only if T01 had not landed); T03 cross-checks the suite against the C1/C2 spec; T04 asserts all 5 green under A4/A5.
